incidents.name: Pickle Finance ControllerV4 fake-jar swap
incidents.notes: ControllerV4.swapExactJarForJar validated only approvedJarConverters for the call targets and never checked that _fromJar/_toJar were Pickle jars, so an attacker-deployed fake jar turned the controller into an arbitrary-call proxy that withdrew the real DAI strategy's cDAI.

sources.ref: onchain review: I read the verified ControllerV4 source at 0x6847259b - swapExactJarForJar only requires approvedJarConverters[_targets[i]], with no jar whitelist; contract created 2020-10-23 by 0xf00d98806a785bb0e1854a0ccc8a39c9c4f4316a, not by attack sender 0xbac8a476; loss of 19,759,355 DAI counted 1:1 in USD. Recheck (deployment basis confirmed): ControllerV4's runtime is unchanged - identical keccak(eth_getCode) at the creation block 11109198 and the incident block 11303123 - and it holds no implementation slot. The single DELEGATECALL taken in the exploit goes to the jar converter 0x6186e99d9cfb05e1fdf1b442178806e81da21dd8, which the same Pickle deployer 0xf00d98806a785bb0e1854a0ccc8a39c9c4f4316a created 278 s after the controller (block 11109222) and whitelisted in approvedJarConverters (mapping at slot 11) 288 s after it (block 11109224, 2020-10-23T00:09:04Z), verified by binary-searching eth_getStorageAt on keccak(converter . 11) - the same deployment session, and worth 288 s out of a 2.57 M-second age, so deployment remains the basis.
